title: Who's Your Caddy?
full_review:
"Who's Your Caddy?" (MGM) is a witless attempt at comedy about a rap mogul named C-Note (Antwan Patton, Big Boi of Outkast) and his entry into a South Carolina country club where his late father had been a caddy.

As it turns out, his father also had set the club's record golf score, a recognition denied his dad because of racism. But director Ron Paul, who co-wrote the script with Bradley Allenstein and Robert Henny, fails to either develop that theme in depth, or even passably mimic the competent pacing of "Caddyshack" or "Happy Gilmore."

Instead, he puts a likable cast through a series of uninspired sequences contrasting raucous hip-hop behavior with sedate and clueless white elites (for some unexplained reason, always male), as per the film's advertising slogan of "it's the street versus the elite."

C-Note is shown to be a Dartmouth graduate with business acumen and negotiating skill, but he buys his way into the club by purchasing a property that includes the 17th hole, and has most of his scenes in blinged-out golfing attire, playing straight man to his buffoonish entourage.

Jeffrey Jones, in his familiar villain persona as country club president Cummings, does most of the heavy lifting, doing comic pratfalls like falling into manure and having Big Large (Faizon Love) fall on top of him. Big Large gets other laughs through extended flatulence.

Sherri Shepherd as Lady G, a member of C-Note's entourage, and Tamala Jones as Shannon, a lawyer hired to thwart the rapper, manage to offset the stereotypical behavior the men exhibit.

The film contains skimpy costuming in a brief filming of a hip-hop video, marijuana fed to a horse, some crude language, fleeting use of the n-word, partial female nudity, rear male nudity, some mild sexual banter and frequent scatological humor. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
